cards.front: A single pass must build all running totals. How do you calculate prefix sum y[i] from the previous prefix sum?

cards.front: A problem needs a running product instead of a running sum. Which operations can a scan accumulate besides addition?
cards.finding: Its example is a running product, which no problem of the unit needs; smallest-stable-index-i needs a running maximum and a suffix minimum, which he computed per index with Math.max(...slice) before the theory. Not tested post-theory; the rewrite aims it at that case.

cards.front: A problem adds up all prefix sums of n inputs. How do you calculate the number of prefix sums y[0] to y[n-1] that contain x[i]?
cards.finding: Taught after sum-of-all-odd-length-subarrays, where he already counted each element's share; its n - i is one factor of the count that problem needs. Keep as the stepping stone to the new subarray-share card.

new_cards.front: One pass keeps the running sum left of a[0] through a[i]. How do you get the sum after index i without a second loop?

new_cards.front: An n-element array is cut into a non-empty left part and a non-empty right part. Which indexes i can end the left part?
new_cards.back: i from 0 through n - 2, written i < n - 1; i = n - 1 would leave the right part empty.
new_cards.why: count-partitions-with-even-sum-difference looped to i < n and counted a split with an empty right side. The deck's off-by-one cards cover the end of a range, not the number of cut points.

new_cards.front: Many ranges [s, e], ends included, each cover points s through e. How does one prefix-sum pass count the cover of every point?
new_cards.back: Write diff[s] += 1 and diff[e + 1] -= 1 for each range, then prefix-sum diff: the running total at a point is its cover count.
new_cards.why: The unit files points-that-intersect-with-cars under prefix sums, but no card links ranges to a prefix sum; the inverse card stops at recovering x. new_cards.why: He had the contribution idea before the theory but reached the count by trial on the judge: 3 wrong answers, the last one missing the division by 2. The only contribution card counts prefix sums (n - i), not subarrays through an index.
